cards.text: Picture it, friend. The exiles are back from captivity, and they've just laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem (Ezra 3:10-11). Then the Bible says the enemies of Judah and Benjamin hear that the exiles are building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.
So they walk right up to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1), and the heads of the families. And they did NOT come empty-handed, friend: they came with an offer.

cards.question: The enemies of Judah and Benjamin come to Zerubbabel and the family heads with an offer. What is it?

answers.text: To pay for the cedar logs

cards.question: True or false: Making their offer, they say they've been sacrificing to Israel's God ever since a king of Assyria brought them there.

cards.text: Zerubbabel, Jeshua the priest (Ezra 3:2) and the other heads of the families hear them out. Then it's their turn to answer.

cards.question: What do Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the family heads tell the people offering to help build?

answers.text: You have no part in this

cards.question: Zerubbabel and the family heads say they alone must build the house for the LORD, as ___ king of Persia commanded them.

cards.text: The people of the land just heard no. Some folks hear no and go home, but these folks change their whole approach.

cards.question: After hearing no, the people of the land change their approach. What do they set out to do to the people of Judah?

answers.text: Tax them for using the land

cards.text: Then they hire counselors against Judah to frustrate their plans. That's like paying somebody a FULL salary just to walk in every morning and unplug my oven.

cards.question: The hired counselors keep frustrating Judah's plans from the reign of Cyrus all the way down to the reign of which king?

cards.text: That's Darius, king of Persia, one king after another. That's a LOT of mornings somebody unplugs my oven, friend.
Now the Bible moves on through the kings of Persia. At the beginning of the reign of Xerxes, an accusation is lodged against the people of Judah.
Then in the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and their associates write him a letter, written in Aramaic and then translated. Friend, these folks are NOT playing.

cards.question: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe write a letter to King Artaxerxes. What city is it against?

cards.text: Rehum and Shimshai's letter opens with a LONG list of who it's from: judges, officials, the Elamites of Susa, and the peoples the great and honorable Ashurbanipal, king of Assyria, deported and settled in Samaria, all calling themselves the king's servants west of the Euphrates. That's the birthday card at work where the whole office signs and nobody can find room to write.
Then the letter gets to the point. It tells the king the Jews who came from him have returned to Jerusalem and are rebuilding it, restoring its walls and repairing its foundations.

cards.question: In their letter to King Artaxerxes, Rehum and Shimshai call Jerusalem that ___ and wicked city.
Next the letter warns the king about what happens if Jerusalem is rebuilt. What do Rehum and Shimshai say the Jews will stop paying?

cards.text: They say they're only writing because it's not fitting for them to let the king be dishonored. That's the coworker who CCs your boss on everything and signs off, "Just looking out for the team!"

cards.question: Rehum and Shimshai want the king to believe Jerusalem has always been trouble. How do they say he can check?
Their big finish: if Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls restored, the king will have no ___ west of the Euphrates.

cards.text: King Artaxerxes writes back and says their letter was translated and read in his presence. The WHOLE thing, friend, and I can't get anybody to read a recipe card past the word "preheat."

cards.question: King Artaxerxes issues a decree and a search is made. What does it turn up about Jerusalem?

answers.text: It revolted against kings long ago
It had never been ruled by kings
It had always lived in peace

cards.question: True or false: King Artaxerxes also says mighty kings once ruled over Jerusalem and were paid tribute.
King Artaxerxes orders Rehum and Shimshai to make the men rebuilding Jerusalem ___.
True or false: King Artaxerxes says Jerusalem can never be rebuilt, no matter what.

cards.text: Then the king tells them not to neglect this matter. That's the boss who ends every email with "Let's not drop the ball on this."

cards.question: King Artaxerxes's letter is read to Rehum, Shimshai and their associates. What do they do?

answers.text: Go to Jerusalem and stop the work by force
Wait a whole year and then send word
Write the king back asking for details

cards.question: So the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem stops. How long does it stay at a standstill?

answers.text: Until the second year of Darius
Until the tenth year of Cyrus
Until the first year of Xerxes

cards.text: So the work sits still, right where they left it. But keep that apron on, friend, because this story is NOT done.
